text:
jess: Heads up — p99 for /chat/generate spiked from ~420ms to ~1.4s around 11:28 UTC. Noticed a small cluster of long-context requests (~6k-8k prompt tokens) plus repeated function/tool calls from the same session. Filing a quick thread to capture traces and hypotheses.

omar: Got the alert. Do we have a profiler dump from the window?

jess: Attached the lightweight profiler snapshot I grabbed from the host (trimmed). Quick paste: 
```
time=11:28:12 route=/chat/generate model=rw-13B-optimized
requests=18 total_tokens=~72k
microbatch_size=12 batching_window_ms=12
kernel_pick: seq<=512 -> fused-attn-v2 ; seq>512 -> fallback-matmul
KV_cache_hit_rate: 78% before spike -> 41% during spike
latency_p50=210ms p95=610ms p99=1.38s
outlier_sessions: 3 sessions with repeated tool calls (loop depth 4-7)
GPU_time dominated by matmul fallback on large seqs
```

sasha: KV hit rate halving is suspicious. Could be prefix eviction when many long prompts come in — we saw similar in weeklies when cache TTL was lowered. Any recent changes to cache shard size?

ryan: I pushed a kernel heuristic tweak yesterday that prefers the generic matmul path for sequences above 1k because we saw numeric regressions on the fused-attn kernel at borderline lengths. Might be related. Reverting is quick if we confirm.

maria: Also saw a pile-up in the microbatching queues — when tool-calls happen we stall token emission while waiting for external call results and the runtime accumulates requests. That increases effective seq length seen by the kernel selection (we pad to max in the batch).

omar: Good point. So two interacting effects: (1) tool-call induced stall -> batches include long contexts/padded sequence lengths -> kernel chooses slower path ; (2) cache eviction or reduced hit-rate making the model re-run KV material for prefixes. Together they blow up p99.

jess: I captured a sample session that reproduces the behavior: user sends ~6k tokens, model emits a tool call -> tool returns -> model resumes and issues another tool call, and this repeats. The pipeline shows repeated full-attn recompute because KV lookups are being garbage-collected mid-session. Snippet: 
```
[session 0x7f8] recv prompt (len=6200) -> kernel choose=matmul_fallback
generate -> emits TOOL_CALL(search) -> pause awaiting tool (200ms)
resume -> batch now includes another short req, pad to 6200 -> kernel still matmul_fallback
KV_CACHE: evict shard 3 due to mem-pressure -> subsequent tokens require recompute
loop count: 5 -> p99 jumps
```

sasha: Do we have memory pressure logs? evict shard 3 suggests the cache reclamation is kicking in. Also check TTL config we shipped last month (we reduced per-shard capacity by 20% for multi-tenant safety).

ryan: I can revert the kernel heuristic and flip an A/B on the microbatching cap. Proposed quick mitigations: 
- revert heuristic (prefer fused-attn for up to 2k seq)
- reduce max_microbatch_size to 8 for p95-sensitive customers
- increase KV per-shard soft-limit by 15% for the canary pool

maria: For the tool-call behavior, we should consider treating tool-call pauses as "sticky" for batching: when a request pauses for external tool, mark it so we don't let its long context inflate other batches (i.e., keep it out of shared microbatches until resume).

omar: Agree. That change is moderate — we need to track backpressure effects but it would avoid padding other requests to the long sequence.

jess: Small repro script that simulates the loop (if anyone wants to run locally): 
```python
# simulate repeated tool calls that pause generation
for i in range(5):
    send_prompt(long_context)
    wait_for_tool()  # 150-300ms
    resume_generation()
```

omar: I ran a quick local canary: revert of kernel heuristic reduced p99 on the simulated workload from 1.4s -> 520ms, and KV hit rate returned to ~75%.

ryan: Deploy plan: revert heuristic to canary pool now, roll microbatch cap change to 10% of hosts for 30m, and toggle per-shard KV soft-limit for that pool. If metrics look good, expand.

perf-bot: deploy started by ryan at 11:46 UTC to canary pool (hosts: c-pool-3).

deploy-bot: canary health check: p99 -> 560ms, KV_hit 73% , error_rate nominal.

jess: Nice. Action items: 
- ryan: canary revert + microbatch cap rollout (in progress)
- sasha: audit last month's KV capacity change and open PR to tune default soft-limits
- maria: prototype "sticky pause" flag for tool-call requests to exclude them from shared microbatches
- omar: follow up with numeric test on fused-attn kernel for 1k-2k boundary (ensure correctness)

maria: I'll put up a draft RFC for sticky pauses, should reduce p99 without losing throughput for normal short requests.

omar: One more note — add a perf histogram by sequence-length buckets (0-256,256-1k,1k-4k,4k+) in the runtime dashboard. We keep needing that to spot these interactions. :eyes:

jess: Agreed. Thanks everyone. Reopen if canary flips or we see regressions. :thumbsup:
